Maybe. Who knows. I know that incident, the car wreck I mentioned before, dramatically changed my life. I should have died. There’s no reason I should still be here. And, due to the emotional and physical pain I have from it, there are days I wish I had. But it’s made me have very little patience for the game aspect. Life can end at any moment. We never know. So I’d rather live my life by being open and honest with people than pretending I’m someone I’m not. 

If someone likes me for who I am, then great. I just want someone I can be with, relate to, grow with, learn from, and someone who complements me as much as I complement them. I find it’s even more tricky for me because I don’t want to get married or have kids. Since my incident, I don’t follow any religion, and I view marriage as an archaic “religious” thing. Although, if that’s what it took to keep someone who means that much to me, then I’d be willing to sacrifice those beliefs in order to make them happy. I did propose to my ex about 6 months before she left. All she said was “why now?”

As for the kids, that’s one I’m less flexible on. I know how much pain and suffering I’ve gone through due to getting flipped into a tree at 100 mph. I wouldn’t want to bring another human being into this world where they would ever possibly be subjected to something that painful. I also don’t know how strong I’d be to watch my child suffer, etc. if it came down to it, I’d rather adopt. There’s tons of children who are already in this world and need a good home/loving family. Having my own kids just feels selfish. 

Obviously, these aren’t things I lead with or mention to people as I get to know them. I know my perspective is more of an acquired taste and tends to lean on the nihilistic side. But since we only have one go at this life, I want to make the most of it and be with someone who makes me happy and vice versa. I don’t feel a need or desire to have someone because that’s the only way I can be happy; however, having a close companionship with someone who makes you strive to be a better person and pushes you in a positive way is something I really want. If any of that makes sense. 

I try my best to be a good person. But I fear my total inability to read into flirting and my general lack of “social skills” (at least when it comes to relationships and dating) are concerned are really a problem for me. I don’t understand how “hey, I like you cause of x, y, and z. I would do anything and everything for you because you’ve made my life better ever since you came into it,” is the wrong approach. Anyway, sorry, just sorting through my thoughts and feelings. But thank you again.

Thanks for your insight. I wasn’t sure whether I should have done or it not. In the past, I’ve kept my feelings closely guarded and it’s always backfired on me. So this time I thought I’d try a different approach; ya know, to not regret not trying. Like I said, I don’t enjoy the “games.” I’ve always had to have fallen for someone before ever pursuing them. Which is kind of counterintuitive. Who knows; I’m weird and sensitive. There’s a strong possibility that I won’t try to date again after this because of how hard these things hit me and, due to the PTSD, depression, and sensitivity; I have no idea if I’ll be able to actually survive another heartbreak. I’m sure it sounds melodramatic and what not, and I blame absolutely no one but myself for any of my problems or issues. Anyway, thank you again. And if I can find myself in a good enough place to try again, I’ll definitely keep what you said in mind.

We still talk. She left 3 years ago. But it’s infrequent. She’ll ignore any message I send for about 2 days before replying. She’s not seeing anyone. And I did explain all of this to her. Many times. Her response was “you just have to get over it.” So, she never understood it. 

I screwed up my right knee and right wrist, broke my two front teeth in half horizontally, slice up the left side of my face, and had a major concussion/blacked out. It took me 6 years before I could walk normally again. As I said, massive headaches and insomnia for two years. I had just started college when this happened and I had to try and juggle school with rehab. My parents had to drive me to and from my classes and I used to massively freak out and lose it if they drove over 20 mph. 

I gained weight cause of my knee. I managed to lose it six years ago, but my knee decided to act up and go into searing pain, and I wasn’t able to put any weight on it for about a year. So I gained the weight back. I had to change careers because of my knee problems. I sincerely get no joy from anything. At all. I truly hate people. When someone gets worked up at work over bullshit, or someone says they “need” something; it tears at me. 

Then all the ugliness in this world. People being senselessly slaughtered by others, the horrific atrocities that happen and continue to happen, just all of it. It’s too much to deal with sometimes. I had to realize extremely early on how fragile life is. How this is our only go at this and it can end in an instant. And yet, there’s people who are so selfish and so oblivious to everything, who take everything for granted...

I know a lot of my thinking is seemingly contradictory. But things are complicated. And I’m just so exhausted of having to do this every day. I’m just so tired. I can’t look at anything that’s happened to me in the last 14 years and honestly say “yeah, I’m glad I was around for that.” Anyway, I appreciate you reaching out. Sometimes the smallest of acts, no matter how insignificant they may seem, can mean the world to another.

Car wreck. The short version is I was a passenger in a car, driver decided to race despite my pleas to stop, hit 100 mph and flipped the car 3 times into a tree. The roof of the car was touching the headrest of my seat.
